sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: The diagram shows hypothalamus, pituitary and thyroid with thyroxine in the blood. What does (a) the solid line and (b) the broken line represent?
questions.answer: (a) Solid line: stimulation (TSH-RH and TSH stimulate release of TSH and thyroxine). (b) Broken line: inhibition (negative feedback of high thyroxine on the hypothalamus and pituitary).

questions.q: Complete the labelling of a neuron: (a) Parts that receive impulses (b) Part that carries the impulse away from the cell body.
questions.answer: (a) Dendrites. (b) Axon.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) The space between the membranes of the brain is filled with a fluid called ______. (b) ______ connects the tympanic cavity with the pharynx.
questions.answer: (a) cerebrospinal fluid. (b) Eustachian tube.

questions.q: Match: (a) FSH (b) Testosterone with (i) male hormone (ii) placenta (iii) Graafian follicle (iv) controls blood sugar.
Name the types of reflex: (a) Knee jerk (b) Salivation on seeing food.
questions.answer: (a) Simple reflex. (b) Conditioned reflex.

questions.q: Name the hormone: (a) lowers blood glucose (b) maintains the activity of the corpus luteum in pregnancy.
questions.answer: (a) Insulin. (b) hCG (human chorionic gonadotropin).

questions.q: State true or false: (a) The sympathetic system slows the heart. (b) Rods are sensitive to dim light.
questions.answer: (a) False. (b) True.

questions.q: Name the three layers of the eyeball and the three meninges.
questions.answer: Sclera, choroid and retina; dura mater, arachnoid and pia mater.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Differentiate between the sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous systems (two points).
questions.answer: The sympathetic system prepares the body for emergencies by increasing heart rate and dilating the pupil; the parasympathetic system restores normal conditions by slowing the heart and constricting the pupil.

questions.q: What is a reflex arc? Name its components.
questions.answer: The pathway of a reflex: receptor, sensory neuron, spinal cord (intermediate neuron), motor neuron and effector (muscle or gland).

questions.q: What is the all-or-none principle?
questions.answer: A nerve impulse is initiated only if the stimulus reaches the threshold; then it travels at its own speed and a stronger stimulus does not make it faster.

questions.q: Distinguish between hormones and pheromones.
questions.answer: Hormones act inside the body of the same organism through blood; pheromones are released outside to influence other individuals of the same species.

questions.q: Name the two pituitary lobes and give one hormone of each.
questions.answer: Anterior: growth hormone, TSH; posterior: oxytocin, ADH.

questions.q: What is the function of the yellow spot and the blind spot?
questions.answer: The yellow spot is the place of sharpest vision; the blind spot has no sensory cells and an image falling on it is not seen.

questions.q: Write two functions of the hypothalamus.
questions.answer: It regulates body temperature and body fluids and controls the secretion of the pituitary.

questions.q: Write the functions of insulin and glucagon.
questions.answer: Insulin lowers blood glucose by helping its utilisation and storage as glycogen; glucagon raises blood glucose by breaking glycogen in the liver.

questions.q: What are myopia and hypermetropia? How are they corrected?
questions.answer: Myopia: distant objects blurred as the image falls in front of the retina, corrected by a concave lens. Hypermetropia: near objects blurred as the image falls behind the retina, corrected by a convex lens.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Draw a neat diagram of the vertical section of the human eye and label the three layers of the eyeball.
questions.answer: Text diagram: outer sclera (white, tough) continuing as the transparent cornea in front; middle choroid (dark, vascular) forming the iris and ciliary body in front; inner retina with rods and cones, yellow spot and blind spot; also lens, aqueous humour, vitreous humour, pupil and optic nerve.

questions.q: Explain the structure of a neuron.
questions.answer: A cell body with nucleus and Nissl granules, short branched dendrites receiving impulses, a long axon with end branches carrying impulses away and a myelin sheath with nodes of Ranvier.

questions.q: Explain how a nerve impulse is conducted along a nerve fibre.
questions.answer: At rest the outside is positive (polarised). A stimulus makes the membrane permeable to Na+, causing depolarisation at that point; this passes as a wave to the next region while the previous region repolarises by the Na+-K+ pump.

questions.q: Describe the mechanism of hearing.
questions.answer: Sound vibrates the eardrum; the ossicles malleus, incus and stapes carry the vibrations to the oval window; the cochlear fluid moves; the organ of Corti sends impulses by the auditory nerve to the brain.

questions.q: Describe the functions of the adrenal medulla and cortex.
questions.answer: The medulla secretes adrenaline (heart rate, BP and glucose up). The cortex secretes glucocorticoids (glucose from amino acids, stress) and mineralocorticoids (aldosterone: sodium and water retention).

questions.q: Explain the feedback control of thyroid activity.
questions.answer: Hypothalamus releases TSH-RH, which makes the pituitary release TSH, which stimulates the thyroid to secrete thyroxine; high thyroxine inhibits the pituitary and hypothalamus and low thyroxine stimulates them.

questions.q: Write short notes on the disorders due to the thyroid.
questions.answer: Hypothyroidism: simple goitre (iodine lack), cretinism in children and myxoedema in adults; hyperthyroidism: exophthalmic goitre.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Describe the structure and functions of the human brain.
questions.answer: Forebrain: cerebrum (cortex of grey matter, white matter, voluntary actions, thinking), thalamus and hypothalamus; midbrain; hindbrain: cerebellum (balance), pons and medulla (breathing, heartbeat); three meninges and cerebrospinal fluid.

questions.q: Describe the structure of the human eye and explain how we see.
questions.answer: Layers sclera, choroid, retina; lens, iris, humours; light passes through the cornea, aqueous humour, lens and vitreous humour to form an inverted real image on the retina, rods and cones convert it to impulses that go via the optic nerve to the brain, which perceives it upright; accommodation adjusts the lens.

questions.q: Explain the hormones of the pituitary gland with their functions and disorders.
questions.answer: GH (dwarfism, gigantism, acromegaly), TSH, ACTH, FSH, LH, ADH (diabetes insipidus) and oxytocin.

questions.q: Write the differences between nervous and hormonal coordination.
questions.answer: Nervous: electrical impulses and chemical transmitters, rapid, short-lived, localised, can be modified by learning. Hormonal: chemicals in blood, slow, long-lasting, general effect and cannot be modified by learning.

questions.q: Describe the endocrine functions of the pancreas and the disorders of insulin.
questions.answer: Alpha cells glucagon, beta cells insulin, delta cells somatostatin; insulin deficiency causes diabetes mellitus with high glucose, glucose in urine, thirst and weight loss; excess causes hypoglycaemia.
